note: Provenance for everything in this repo that came from somewhere else. `upstream` names where it originates; `via` is the commit it was taken from. `upstream_name` is the directory it occupies upstream when that differs from ours — the drift job resolves by it. `diverged` means our copy differs from upstream on purpose and says why — the weekly drift job flags a marker that no longer matches reality. `note` is history that is not a divergence. `authored_here` marks files written for this marketplace rather than copied. Refresh against upstream by diffing these paths. See ADR 0011.
upstream_mirror_baseline: mattpocock/skills @ main (v1.2.0-dev), mirrored by justinpbarnett/ai@e36ec09. Most skills are still at that baseline; the `via` on each entry is authoritative where it differs. Upstream has since regrouped skills/<name> into skills/<category>/<name>, which is why resolution goes through directory name rather than path.

excluded_skills.ask-matt: Upstream skill about its own author. Not useful here. See ADR 0007.
excluded_skills.contribute: Upstream OSS contribution flow; forks into ~/dev/. No department does this. See ADR 0014.
excluded_skills.handoff: Upstream skill for handing a session to another agent. Dropped 2026-08-06 — nothing references it and no department asked for it. See ADR 0018.
excluded_skills.writing-great-skills: Upstream's guide to writing skills, since renamed writing-for-agents. Dropped 2026-08-06: it served contributors, and contributing is rare enough to read the file in the repo instead of carrying it in everyone's picker. See ADR 0018.
excluded_skills.setup-repo: Upstream's setup-matt-pocock-skills, renamed by ADR 0014. ADR 0015 removed its issue-tracker section once Jira became a given; what remained was a label mapping whose two columns were identical and a doc layout domain-modeling creates lazily anyway. Dropped 2026-08-06. See ADR 0019.

codebase-design.diverged: The ASCII depth diagrams are removed: they drew a large implementation under a small interface, which is the lines-of-code ratio the skill's own 'Rejected framings' section bans.

diagnosing-bugs.diverged: Skill pointers namespaced to `/plugin:skill` — upstream is one flat directory where `/x` resolves; here it does not (CI check `cross-references`). prototype.note: Refreshed from upstream 2026-08-05. LOGIC.md now produces one self-contained HTML file with guided walkthroughs instead of a terminal TUI — the reason to take it here, since Ops, Analytics and Service and Support are the people a prototype has to reach.

tdd.diverged: Refreshed from upstream 2026-08-05, plus the one patch that refresh needed: upstream's new `/codebase-design` pointer namespaced to `/dev:codebase-design`.

Skill pointers namespaced to `/plugin:skill` — upstream is one flat directory where `/x` resolves; here it does not (CI check `cross-references`). ticket.notes: SKILL.md rewritten for plugin invocation. fetch_ticket.py repointed at passion_env and at an attachment directory outside every repo (ADR 0001). passion_env.py is new.

sprint.notes: Replaces jira-pull.sh. Rewritten in Python: no jq dependency, no hardcoded project key.

onboard.note: Role-first introduction to the marketplace. Names skills across every plugin by design, so check.py exempts it from the reachability rule via CATALOGUE_FILES. Its recommendation table must be updated when skills are added or removed. See ADR 0018.

rock.notes: One skill for all of Rock. rock-tools shipped a single rock skill; ADR 0013 split it into nine across two plugins, and ADR 0023 merged it back to one on the report that nine commands was more than anyone could hold. Reads and the safety rules are in SKILL.md; references/writing.md holds the write loop and every operation; references/connection.md the setup, catalog, exception logs and browser opt-in; references/lava.md the template guidance. action-types.md and block-types.md carried a stale repo-relative catalog path (`data/rock/catalog.json`) and now point at `~/.claude/passion-rock/catalog.json` (ADRs 0001, 0016); lava-reference.md is copied unchanged. The group operations and api_request were authored here, not vendored — see ADR 0022.

runtime.note: Executable code ported from rock-tools. Unlike the skills, this is largely the original source with targeted patches. See ADRs 0003, 0004, 0016, 0023.

patched: ROCK_ALLOW_WRITES guard on the four write subcommands (ADRs 0016, 0023); PATCH instead of PUT in person-update, and the query-string attribute route in block-set (ADR 0022)
files.plugins/rock/runtime/scripts/rock_client: patched: dotenv removed, credentials via passion_env (ADR 0005)
files.plugins/rock/runtime/scripts/passion_env: authored here; identical copy in plugins/jira/skills/*/scripts
files.plugins/rock/runtime/pyproject.toml: rewritten: Playwright moved to an optional group, dev group dropped (ADR 0003)
files.plugins/rock/runtime/uv.lock: generated by `uv lock` from our pyproject, not carried over
patched: PATCH instead of PUT, the query-string attribute route, six group operations and a guarded api_request (ADR 0022). Moved here from plugins/rock-build (ADR 0023)

not_ported.justfile: Recipes were one-line wrappers; rock.sh replaces them (ADR 0004).
not_ported..env.example: Named our Jira and Rock hostnames. Replaced by a template with blank values (ADR 0001).
not_ported..claude/skills/rock/setup.md: Content absorbed into the status skill, sanitised (ADR 0004).
not_ported.CLAUDE.md, README.md, data/: Repo-specific; not part of the plugin.

contaminated_skills.note: Claude Code's own built-ins, written into the source directory by the tool rather than chosen by anyone. Never shippable — see ADR 0007 and the CONTEXT.md definition. CI fails if any of these names appears under plugins/.

refinement_pass: 2026-08 rubric pass: every one of the 31 skills was reviewed against the writing-great-skills rubric (no-ops, duplication, leading words, completion criteria, negation, progressive disclosure). Skills vendored from an upstream therefore diverge from it in wording throughout, beyond what any per-skill `diverged` marker names. Those markers record structural and behavioural divergence — new files, changed contracts, retargeted pointers — not prose. See ADR 0020.
